rows.title: An app call by a principal without resolved permissions is refused
rows.decision: Unify to refusal. Before, isAppInvocationAllowed (appToolsGateway.js) let every caller through that carried no permissions object, so such a caller could call an app no group grants. Now the gateway fails closed, and the run service refuses any run whose context has no principal with resolved permissions (no run context can be built for one) and any app the principal may not open, with an entry in the audit log. In the golden the caller gets the refusal a user who may not open the app gets ("You do not have permission to access app restricted"); no run starts, so the record has no ledger, model request, offered tool or usage record any more, and the case title says what it pins now. No option to keep the old behaviour: it is a security weakness.

rows.title: An unattended run of an admin no longer carries admin rights
rows.decision: Proposed: unify to "admin rights only while a person is present". A scheduled task, a follow-up or a wake of an owner who is an admin runs with the rights of the groups of the owner and without the admin flags. No option to keep them: an unattended run must not act as an administrator. In the golden the flag shows in one place: the model is offered the tool workflow_installation-check, a workflow of the app that no group of the owner grants and that is offered because an admin may run every workflow (workflowAccess.js). After the change the run offers no tool. The app itself is granted by the group and stays.

rows.title: One rule for how a long tool result is cut, on every surface
rows.decision: Proposed: unify to the rule of the chat turn (the result goes to the model whole, and the compaction condenses it later). Today an app call through the gateway or as a tool also caps the results it collects for its caller at a fixed size. The cap of the collected copy stays as an option of the headless host; the model sees the same text on every surface. Moved to chat-on-run-service (it was attributed to run-service-headless): run-service-headless changes none of these goldens; the cap stays in the headless host as it was. The chat turns and the inference API, whose goldens this row names, move onto the run service in chat-on-run-service, which delivers the one rule.

rows.title: One policy for a call that needs approval where nobody can approve
rows.decision: Proposed: unify to "refuse and tell the model", with the code APPROVAL_REQUIRED_NO_USER, for every run without a person who can answer (app as a tool, MCP, A2A, the inference API). A scheduled task keeps its own route as an option: its run waits for the owner, and a refusal of the owner ends the run as cancelled. Moved to chat-on-run-service (it was attributed to run-service-headless): for the app as a tool and MCP the goldens already record the refusal with APPROVAL_REQUIRED_NO_USER (app-as-tool/approval-denied.json, mcp/approval-refused.json), and run-service-headless keeps it without changing them. The inference API and the scheduled task move onto the run service in chat-on-run-service, which settles the rest of the row.

rows.title: The text a model gets for a failed or refused tool call is the same on every surface
rows.decision: Proposed: unify to the text of the chat turn. Today the chat turn, the app call and the gateway word the same refusal differently (a tool that is not registered, a refused approval, a refused question). The codes stay as they are; only the message text changes. Moved to chat-on-run-service (it was attributed to run-service-headless): run-service-headless leaves every text this row names as it was, and none of these goldens changes. The chat turn moves onto the run service in chat-on-run-service, where the texts of the chat, the app call and the gateway become one.

rows.title: When a long tool loop condenses its context
rows.decision: Proposed: unify to the trigger of the chat turn (half of the context window of the model, at least 16,000 tokens, with a findings digest) for every surface that runs on the run service. Today only the chat turn uses the digest; a headless run shortens old results to previews. The preview strategy stays as an option of a run.

rows.title: One limit for the rounds of a tool loop
rows.decision: Proposed: keep as an option per run, with one default. Today the limit of rounds and of wall-clock time differs by surface (a chat turn, an app call with its 3-minute clock, a scheduled run). The run service takes both from the budget of the run; the defaults of today stay, so no golden should change. This row is for the case that one does.

rows.title: A stopped run says why it stopped in the same words on every surface
rows.decision: Proposed: unify to the abort cause of the chat turn (a kind, who, from where). Today a stopped chat turn names its cause; a disconnected call of the inference API and a stopped headless run record only that they were aborted. The stored finish reason of a chat answer does not change.

rows.title: A usage record names the origin of its run and, for an agent, the agent
rows.decision: Proposed: additive. Every usage record gains the origin of the run (person, schedule, sub-agent, gateway) and the id of the agent when there is one. Today an app call is recorded with the surface "chat" and is not told apart from a chat turn. No existing field changes its meaning.

rows.title: An evidence record names the actor of the run
rows.decision: Proposed: additive. The evidence record of an answer gains who acted (the person, or the schedule, sub-agent or gateway that ran for the person) beside the owner it is filed under. Nothing is removed.

rows.title: run/started gains fields; none is removed or renamed
rows.decision: Proposed: additive. The first event of a run gains the fields of the run context (origin, depth, whether a person is present). A client that does not know them ignores them. Every golden with a run changes in the same way, so the row names the plain case of each surface; the pull request that adds the fields lists the others.

rows.title: The tool row of an app call is titled with the name of the app
rows.decision: Unify to the title a sub-agent has, decided on the server: the row of app__<id> is titled with the localized name of the app alone (in the golden "Claims specialist" instead of "App: Claims specialist"), on tool/started and on the ledger's tool/call. The tool definition carries the name for that (appName), so the tool definitions the ledger records gain the field and their hash (toolSchemasHash) changes; what the model is sent does not change (modelRequests and toolSchemas are the same). The activity kind stays tool: the chat has no sub-agent row yet, and the pull request that adds it gives the app call that kind.

rows.title: An app called as a tool works in the scopes the person picked and no longer gets iHub's context as variables
rows.decision: Proposed: unify to the rule of a chat turn (#3925). Before, the tool runner handed an app__<id> call every key of the call except chatId, user, appConfig and language as arguments, so the integration scopes the person picked in the calling chat, the turn's skill log and the person's timezone became variables of the called app, and a call without a message sent all three to the called app's model as its message (JSON of the arguments); the called app ran without a scope binding. Now the model's arguments alone become the app's message and variables; the scopes and the timezone travel beside them: the called app works in the picked scopes where it uses the same integration (resolveChatScopes; a scope the person may not use in the called app refuses the call, as it refuses a chat turn), and its tools get the timezone. No golden records it: app-as-tool/ok.json calls with a message and without scopes, so its model requests are the same; server/tests/appToolsGateway.test.js pins the new behaviour. No option to keep the old behaviour: it leaked the caller's context into another app's prompt.

rows.title: The tool definitions a run records carry the declared side effect of iHub's own tools
rows.decision: Proposed: accept as an added field. Every shipped and internal tool now declares what it does (sideEffect), and the run ledger records the tool definitions of a model request as they are. In these goldens three tools gain the field: recall_tool_result (read) in the compaction cases, read_memory (read) and write_memory (write) in the scheduled runs with notes. The hash over the recorded definitions (toolSchemasHash) and the evidence record of the same request change with it. Nothing the model is sent changes (modelRequests and toolSchemas are the same), no event is added, removed or moved, and no approval is asked or dropped in a golden. No option to keep the old record: a tool without a declaration would be an undeclared tool again.
